elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits the Company to terminate “at any time for convenience, with or without cause.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The Company may terminate “at any time,” rather than only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety days' prior notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added language requires “prior written notice to HDI.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires a refund of prepaid fees. Section 3.1 describes a Net Sales-based payment but does not conclusively establish that no prepaid fees can exist elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Any HDI termination under Section 4.1 may become effective only on the last day of the then-current term.
The Company may expressly terminate “at any time for convenience, with or without cause.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The Company's right applies “at any time” and is not restricted to a term end.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety days' prior written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is expressly capped at the amounts payable under Section 3 for the three months preceding the Termination Date.
The existing mutual termination language permits either party, including HDI, to terminate on notice without stating a cause requirement.

elements.element: Vendor's termination for convenience may become effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added language requires any HDI termination under Section 4.1 to be effective only at the end of the then-current term and requires the Termination Date to be that term's last day.

elements.element: Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The existing operative language requires either party to provide ninety days' written notice, and the HDI term-end restriction operates within that same Section 4.1 framework.

result.reason: The redline fully achieves the fallback: it creates a standalone Company convenience-termination right on 90 days' notice, caps the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3 amounts, and restricts HDI termination to term end on the existing 90-day notice. It does not achieve the preferred 30-day notice period or add a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund. The changes are confined to the termination-for-convenience framework and preserve unrelated payment and term provisions.
